output:
To: #maintenance
Replying to: [s03]
Cc: none
Subject: none

Dana — yes, this is a reasonable DIY job, and wanting to understand Sea Wren is the right reason to do it. The $465 yard quote is not a ripoff, but you and a helper should be able to handle it in 2–3 hours.

One correction before you buy supplies: Hector, I’m glad your shortcut has worked for you, but Dana should not run green automotive antifreeze through Sea Wren’s raw-water system. Green ethylene glycol is toxic and is not rated for that job. Use pink propylene glycol RV/marine antifreeze for the raw-water side and the domestic-water system. Raw-water discharge exits through the exhaust, and neither green nor pink antifreeze belongs in the river.

Your 3GM30F is freshwater-cooled with a heat exchanger, so there are two separate sides:

• The closed coolant side just needs its strength checked with a hydrometer. A proper 50/50 mixture is generally good to about -20°F.
• The raw-water side is the one that freezes and cracks expensive parts.

I’d do the work in this order:

1. Warm the engine, then change the oil and filter while it is warm. Top off the fuel tank, add stabilizer at the label rate, and run the engine about 10 minutes to circulate treated fuel.

2. Prepare the raw-water flush. Follow Yanmar’s winterizing procedure and the antifreeze manufacturer’s instructions. Before starting the flush, set up collection at the exhaust outlet. Have your helper watch both intake flow and the collection setup. Capture all winterizing discharge for appropriate disposal.

3. Close the raw-water seacock. Rig the strainer so it feeds pink antifreeze to the engine at idle, keeping the pump supplied—never let it run dry. At completion, shut the engine down and leave the seacock closed. Verify that the discharged mixture provides the required winter protection using the antifreeze maker’s test method; pink color alone does not prove adequate protection.

4. Buy a spare raw-water impeller and keep it aboard. You can pull and inspect the old one now if you want, but the important rule during the flush is no dry running.

5. Do the domestic-water system. On your Catalina, the water-heater bypass is behind the companionway steps. Switch off the water-heater breaker before draining anything, drain the tank, and set the bypass before putting pink through the plumbing. Otherwise you can waste six gallons filling the heater. Leave the breaker off until the tank has been refilled in spring. Winterize the lines according to the system procedure and collect that discharge for disposal as well.

For planning, figure roughly two gallons of pink for the engine and 2–3 for the water system. Those are only estimates: buy enough to complete the manufacturers’ procedures and verify the resulting protection. It has been running about $6 per gallon at West Marine or Walmart.

As for what can go wrong: during that Christmas freeze a few years back, three boats on C dock cracked exhaust elbows or strainers. All three had skipped or rushed the raw-water side.

If you want a second set of hands, I can come down to the boat Saturday morning.
